newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul Cos earnings hurt by storm losses.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul Cos earnings hurt by storm losses.

text.p: St. Paul Cos Inc, an insurance company group, said Monday its lower operating earnings for the fourth quarter and the year were hurt by large losses from severe storms across the United States in 1996.

"Our operating earnings were adversely impacted by 1996 catastrophe losses of $207 million -- second only to 1992, when Hurricane Andrew devastated the southeastern coast," said Douglas Leatherdale, chairman and chief executive officer.
"However, our results were aided by the excellent performance of our investment portfolio," Leatherdale said.
Leatherdale said pretax investment income exceeded $800 million for the year, and the company also posted record after-tax gains of $143 million from the sale of investments.
St. Paul Cos reported fourth quarter operating earnings of $1.18 a share versus $1.34 for the period last year, and $4.55 for the year versus $5.25 in 1995.

"The insurance industry marketplace remains highly competitive," Leatherdale said. "Still, our domestic underwriting operation's performance was satisfactory, in light of unusually severe catastrophe losses."
